title: MZ Sideview animated battlers controlled using troop commands?

posts.author: VeryPeachy
posts.body:
Heya, I know this question is asked around a ton, but when it comes to making animated enemies for sideview, I would need a plugin that allows me to play separate animations in commands, so I can use it with battle sequences to create QTE's and such with proper timings. (Alongside idle animations and the such) I'm aware of Akea's animated battlers, Battle Flipbooks, and using character spritesheets on enemies using visu's battlecore, but I'm moreso looking for a plugin like Hendrix's animation solution, but for battles. (Also if it could be used on the player characters, that would be sick, but more of a bonus?)
I'm fine to see both paid and free plugins (Or hell even some JS that lets me do this), but I feel like I'm going insane considering how this should be an essential plugin that's like nowhere? I know it must be decently hard to implement (most likely how sideview animation works in the first place), but I've seen this be done...
Any and all help would be appreciated.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body: Sounds like you can just do that with visustella's action sequencing, no?

posts.author: VeryPeachy
posts.body: Playing animations using a spritesheet that's not using a battler's spritesheet? I've looked around, I don't believe that's a function (unless I'm just dumb and can't find it)

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
VeryPeachy said:
Playing animations using a spritesheet that's not using a battler's spritesheet? I've looked around, I don't believe that's a function (unless I'm just dumb and can't find it)
Click to expand...
Not sure I understand the question. An animation that's a sprite sheet but not a battler sprite sheet is simply an animation. You can do MV style animations in MZ by simply right clicking an animation ID and selecting "Create MV-Compatible Data"
That will let you use a spritesheet in 192x192 pixel cells just like MV animations did. If that still can't accomplish what you need, we'll need more details on why that doesn't work.

posts.author: VeryPeachy
posts.body: Ah, I don't mean playing animations. I've been told it's like expedition 33, where the enemy moves up to the player, initiates a swing, and if they press a button at a certain time, they dodge / parry / whatever. I've been looking for a plugin to play custom animations for the enemies, such as a swing, or an idle, or a walk, while in battle, without being confined by the sv_actor spritesheet that I know battle_core allows enemies to use

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
What does confined even mean tho? The sprite displayed is the battler sprite. How would you make it swing if you're planning on not using the battler sprite? I think there are plugins for more battler frames too(At least on MV they had them, not sure about MZ specifically), so I'm really not quite sure why you're trying to somehow circumvent the entire system.
Timed inputs like exp33, legend of dragoon, paper mario and similar can all be achieved with visu's plugins either evented within the common event used in skills or potentially with an additional plugin. I'm on MV myself so I don't know which timed input plugins exist for MZ off the top of my head, but it is possible.
Imho you don't even require more battler frame specifically, as there are plenty of motions already available on one such sheet.
edit: But let's say you still somehow want to not use the actual battler, you can still put your battler's swing animation on an MV style animation sheet and display that instead, so long as you can fit the battler on a 192x192 cell.

posts.body:

QTE's is easy to event. I'm really not worried about all that.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Yeah, you'll need a plugin that let's you use more frames or alternatively call multiple 3 frame motions after one another to achieve a 12 frame swing.
Here's one such plugin:
https://yexinnn.itch.io/framex-extended-frame
You'd then just use visu's action sequencing to make the battler move towards the target, call your motion and it'll play whatever motion you want with the amount of frames you set up. and in there you'll just time your timed input.

posts.author: VeryPeachy
posts.body: Ah, that's very useful! Thank you! I'll look around more for plugins of that sort, it would be nice to be able to pause animations halfway through movements, but that's honestly pretty doable.

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
Yeah you can accommodate that by just having multiple static frames basically. There are ways around it, but ultimately rpg maker just isn't really the type of engine for this stuff specifically and there are only so many free/low cost things you can grab.
If push comes to shove, you can always pay a coder to make a plugin exactly the way you want it.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body: VisuStella action sequences has INJECT command where you can use an additional spritesheet with any number of frames. And it says you can also pause and restart it. They also have time scale and time stop commands.

posts.author: VeryPeachy
posts.body: Ohmygod, that's actually amazing! Thanks so much for telling me!
